name: שברים חלקיים – מונה ממעלה גבוהה, חילוק ומכנה x(2x+a) (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Find

\[ \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} \]

by expressing the integrand in partial fractions.

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: The numerator has a higher degree than the denominator: first divide (long division), then write the remaining proper fraction as a sum of partial fractions, find the coefficients and integrate term by term.
Step 1 — Long division
Since the degree of the numerator is greater than the degree of the denominator we need to use long division to get a simpler form to express

\[ {{CT:0}}. \]

Partial fractions: \( \frac{p(x)}{(x-a)(x-b)}=\frac{A}{x-a}+\frac{B}{x-b} \); a repeated factor \( (x-a)^2 \) gives \( \frac{A}{x-a}+\frac{B}{(x-a)^2} \); an irreducible \( x^2+bx+c \) gives \( \frac{Ax+B}{x^2+bx+c} \)
Using long division we get that

\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:2}} + {{CT:3}} \]

Step 2 — Partial fractions
Now,

\[ {{CT:2}} = {{CT:4}}{{CT:5}} + {{CT:6}}{{CT:7}} \]

So, multiplying by \({{CT:8}}\) both sides we get

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:9}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:10}} + {{CT:11}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:12}} \end{array} \]

So, equating coefficients in \({{CT:1}}\) we get a system of equations that can be solved to get \(A = {{CT:13}}\) and \(B = {{CT:14}}\). Hence,

\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:15}} \]

Step 3 — Integrating term by term
So,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int {{CT:15}} d{{CT:1}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:13}} \int {{CT:5}} d{{CT:1}} + {{CT:14}} \int {{CT:7}} d{{CT:1}} + \int ({{CT:3}}) d{{CT:1}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:16}} + {{CT:17}} + {{CT:18}}+c \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:19}}+c \end{array} \]
